page: Microsoft Azure D4ls_v6 is a low-memory compute instance within the Dlsv6 series, configured on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is driven by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware resources include 2 physical cores hyperthreaded to 4 dedicated vCPUs, backed by 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache. System memory totals 8.0 GB, providing an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction extensions feature AVX-512, AMX matrix acceleration, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The hardware configuration includes no local storage and zero integrated GPUs, relying entirely on remote network-attached disks such as Premium Storage. In computational benchmarks, the high clock frequency and modern architecture deliver strong single-threaded performance, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 2115.0 and strong text processing throughput. Multi-core and bandwidth metrics reflect the 4-vCPU and 8.0 GB capacity limits, showing average Geekbench multi-core results of 4761.0, an average PassMark CPU score of 7382.74, and weak uncached large-block memory bandwidth alongside lower throughput in parallel software compilation.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio lowers hypervisor resource overhead for compute-focused services that do not require standard 1:4 memory allocations. The primary tradeoff lies in the lack of local temporary storage and constrained memory footprint, which bounds working set sizes. Microsoft Azure D4ls_v6 is appropriately sized for static web serving, microservices, batch processing, single-threaded application routines, and small-model CPU inference pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ls_v6 is a compute-focused general purpose virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 8.0 GB of memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor incorporates advanced vector and matrix capabilities including AVX-512 and AMX. This server includes no local disk storage, requiring remote storage solutions, and contains no dedicated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show strong single-core computational execution, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2115.0, alongside moderate multi-threaded and static web serving capabilities. System memory bandwidth and multi-core compilation show lower relative performance due to resource density boundaries. The D4ls_v6 is well matched for lightweight compute tasks, static web serving, API endpoints, microservices, and small-scale machine learning inference workloads.
